- issues opened in `idea-repo`#3 ("Review of the Brief: floor definition, equal-terms arms, validity protocol, prior work") by `idea-review-repo`  > # Review 1 of the Brief (idea-review) — strengthening requests, ordered by importance
  > 
  > Read: `Brief` wiki page, `prior_work.md`, `commitment.md` at idea-repo `4ddc0fd`, against the objective (TASK.md, deliverable.md, data.md).
  > 
  > ## What is strong (keep)
  > - The question is the objective's question, answered on both sides ("how much" *and* "where no room"); "PPI++ is already near the floor" is explicitly allowed as the finding.
  > - Honest positioning: credits Zhang–Brown–Cai / DML/AIPW and refuses to claim a new efficiency principle. Keep this; it is what makes the paper defensible.
  > - Decomposition classical → PPI++ → floor with learning cost separated, paired width ratio vs PPI++, MC CIs on coverage, ablations, synthetic with known truth, falsifiable expectations. Good.
  > 
  > ## Weaknesses and what would fix them
  > 
  > **1. The "floor" is under-specified and, as written, partly wrong for this setting (most important).**
  >  a. The efficient estimator under MCAR averages g(Z) over *all* n+N records (labeled records also carry Z), then adds mean_lab(Y−g): variance σ²_res/n + V_g/(n+N), σ²_res=E Var(Y|Z), V_g=Var E[Y|Z]. The Brief's formula Var(Y−g)/n + Var(g)/N is the unlabeled-only form, and `ppi_mean_ci` uses only unlabeled f for the mean. So even with g=g* that form is above the bound by V_g(1/N − 1/(n+N)). When n is a non-trivial fraction of N (the grid goes to "several thousand" labels on pools of 1.6k–17k) this is a free, calibration-independent gain, and it must be a separate step in the decomposition (classical → PPI++ → PPI++ with pooled Z → calibrated g → floor), otherwise "gain from calibration" is confounded with "gain from using labeled Z". Please derive the bound yourselves and state it.
  >  b. The floor is conditional on the information set: floor(f) = E Var(Y|f) vs floor(f,X). Report them as two tiers; "headroom" is only claimable for f-only on the 6 non-census sets.
  >  c. E[Y|Z] is unknown; the floor can only be *estimated* (cross-fitted fit on the full pool) and is then a floor within a model class. Say so, report its uncertainty, and note it is poor for `forest` (1596) and `ballots` (1027 labels).
  >  d. A clean closed form is available and is probably the paper's best theoretical item: PPI++'s excess variance over the floor is E[(E[Y|f] − a* − b* f)²] (best-linear-approximation gap, Pythagoras), against a learning cost of order d_eff·σ²_res/n. This gives a predicted break-even n and a labels-only diagnostic of headroom (with its own CI) that an analyst can compute. Make that, plus a "no room" condition (E[Y|f] affine ⇒ PPI++ is optimal; Gaussian synthetic case), a stated proposition checked against experiments. It turns the contribution from "we ran AIPW" into an answer to "when yes, when no".
  > 
  > **2. Novelty of contribution 2 is thin; make the claim the one that is true.** A K-fold cross-fitted AIPW/DML interval for a mean with known MCAR propensity is textbook; the Brief itself lists it as a baseline. Present it as the instrument, not the contribution. Also note a point that is better than the Brief states: because the labeling propensity is known (MCAR), validity needs only that ĝ converges to *some* fixed limit in L2, not that it is consistent for E[Y|Z]; a bad calibrator costs width, not coverage. State this with the proof sketch; it is the "valid" half of the answer.
